newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Sing dlr up on ringgit liquidation.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Sing dlr up on ringgit liquidation.

text.p: The Singapore dollar rose in Monday morning trade as players unwound long dollar/Sing and Malaysian ringgit/Sing positions following weekend comments by Singapore's Finance Minister Richard Hu.
Hu said the Singapore dollar could be expected to maintain its more modest rise of recent years if the global inflationary environment remained favourable.
Hu repeated Singapore's policy objective of having a strong currency to shield against foreign inflationary pressures.

"To me, his comments look quite ambiguous but basically the market was long dollar/Sing and the ringgit/Sing cross so they just took it as an excuse to unwind their positions," a U.S. bank dealer said.
He said local banks sold dollar/Sing down aggressively from an opening 1.4450/55, but added that bids from U.S. funds appeared to be providing some support around 1.4410/15.
"I think we'll stay around here for a while and see if London wants to take it lower. There are some stops building below the 1.4400 level," he added.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4415/25 to the U.S. dollar at 0425 GMT. The ringgit/Sing cross was at 0.5812/18 against its opening 0.5830.
A Japanese bank dealer said the market could have interpreted Hu's comments as signalling that the Sing dollar's recent decline had been too rapid.
But he said players had merely been taking profit on their long ringgit/Sing positions and there had been no real shift in market sentiment favouring the cross.
The Malaysian ringgit remained in its recent tight band as dollar buying interest by Kuala Lumpur banks around 2.4770 came up against offers from New York parties above 2.4790.
Dealers said the market was awaiting the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy-making meeting for an indication of the U.S. interest rate outlook.
Anticipation of Bank Negara Malaysia's annual report on Friday also limited activity.
Any confirmation the central bank intended to keep its monetary policy tight due to still-strong money supply growth would help the ringgit, dealers said.
In Indonesia, the rupiah firmed amid expectations of tighter liquidity due to higher tax payments at the financial year end on March 31.
Jakarta dealers said short-dated swaps remained stable, but one-week and one-month money indicated some uptrend as operators also prepared for a new reserve requirement rate from April 16.
A local bank dealer said offshore players continued to sell the dollar on persistent speculation of another widening of the central bank's intervention band.
Spot rupiah was at 2,403.00/04.00 at 0425 GMT against an opening of 2,404.75/05.75.
"There's some speculation of a band widening again. We've seen a lot of selling of dollars out of Jakarta itself," said the U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.

He said the dollar was likely to be capped at 2,404.50/05.00 and could head downwards to test 2,402.00. The Thai baht gained from the dollar's weakness against the majors but ample money market liquidity limited the baht's upside, Bangkok dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 25.949-25.952 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 25.970-25.975 late on Friday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.94 per dollar against 25.97 on Friday.
"The market is still taking long dollar positions despite the U.S. unit's weakness abroad. Ample liquidity prompted people to hold the dollar," a foreign bank dealer said.
Expectations of a dollar rebound if the Fed went ahead and hiked rates on Tuesday, as is widely expected, also underpinned the dollar against the baht, he said.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 7.50-8.00 percent early compared with 7.00-8.00 late on Friday.
-- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
